positions.name: CalibrationGroundedInReferenceVerification
positions.frame: what establishes that the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration is sound — verification against a fixed reference standard?
positions.why: All three expressions converge on the same directional read: the calibration's validity rests on having been checked against the June reference plates, not on the calibration figure alone. src-1 states this as flat, unhedged prose ('now calibrated', 'verified... against the June reference plates', 'holds across the full observing band'); src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument and calibration fact in labeled-field form under fc-1 footing, with src-3 explicitly repeating the verification-against-reference-plates language. The register pass marks all three with the same flat, jargon-native, matter-of-fact signature (mint-1, FlatTechnicalLogbook); the power and value reads independently converge on expert/informational authority grounded in competence — verification against a named standard is the appealed-to good throughout. Held together: a competence claim (accuracy) and its evidentiary anchor (the reference plates) — no tension, just one claim stated three ways at different structural registers.
